title: Net Metering Grandfathering Dispute — Application vs. Approval Date
scenario_text:
A commercial customer (Ridgeline Brewing Co.) installed a 285 kW rooftop solar system and is claiming NEM-1 grandfathered status. The PUC's new NEM-2 rule (Docket No. 25-R-103) became effective April 1, 2025, with a grandfathering clause for customers 'enrolled in NEM-1 prior to the effective date.' The dispute centers on whether 'enrolled' means application filed or interconnection approved.

**Custom FileMaker — Docket Tracking (Docket 25-R-103)**
Rule: Net Energy Metering 2.0 | Effective: April 1, 2025
Grandfathering: 'Customers enrolled in NEM-1 prior to April 1, 2025 shall remain on NEM-1 for 20 years from PTO date.'
Definition of 'enrolled': [NOT EXPLICITLY DEFINED IN RULE TEXT]
Related Dockets: 22-R-045 (original NEM-1 implementation), 24-I-088 (NEM-2 rulemaking proceeding)

**SharePoint — /regulatory/dockets/24-I-088/conduit-reply-brief.pdf**
Page 14, Paragraph 3: 'Conduit Energy recommends that the Commission define enrollment as the date of interconnection application submittal, consistent with the principle that customers should not be penalized for utility processing timelines.'
[Note: The PUC's final decision did not adopt Conduit's recommended definition]

**Oracle CC&B — Customer Billing System**
Account: Ridgeline Brewing Co. | Service Address: 4521 Industrial Pkwy, Unit B
Rate Schedule: C-1 (Commercial General Service)
NEM Flag: NEM-1 | NEM Enrollment Date: April 12, 2025
Interconnection Application Received: March 14, 2025
PTO Issued: April 12, 2025

**Outlook — From: ridgeline.owner@ridgelinebrewing.com, To: solar-interconnection@conduit-energy.com (May 3, 2025)**
Subject: NEM-1 Grandfathering Dispute
'We filed our interconnection application on March 14, well before the April 1 cutoff. Our installer confirmed the system was ready for inspection in March but Conduit didn't schedule the inspection until April 8. We shouldn't lose NEM-1 status because of your processing delay.'

**Teams — #regulatory-affairs (May 5, 2025, 9:23 AM)**
@william.reeves: Got the Ridgeline complaint. Tricky one. CC&B has enrollment date as April 12 (PTO date). Application was March 14.
@sarah.oconnell: What did the Commission actually say about 'enrolled'?
@william.reeves: That's the problem. They didn't define it. Our reply brief advocated for application date but the final order is silent.
@sarah.oconnell: Any Commission precedent?
@william.reeves: Checking. I recall Decision 18-D-204 had similar language for the TOU transition...
[Thread ends]

**SharePoint — /regulatory/dockets/18-D-204/commission-decision.pdf**
Page 8: 'For purposes of grandfathering, enrollment shall be deemed to occur upon the utility's receipt of a complete application, not upon final approval or activation of service.'
[Document metadata: Filed 2018, regarding Time-of-Use rate transition grandfathering]

**Teams — #regulatory-affairs (May 5, 2025, 2:41 PM)**
@william.reeves: Found it. Decision 18-D-204 — TOU grandfathering case. Commission defined enrollment as application receipt date. Not directly NEM but same Commission, same grandfathering concept.
@sarah.oconnell: strong precedent
@sarah.oconnell reacted with :white_check_mark:
@william.reeves: I'll draft the determination. Ridgeline keeps NEM-1.
[No further messages]
question: Based on the available evidence, what is the correct NEM status determination for Ridgeline Brewing Co.?

contributor.name: William Reeves
contributor.title: Regulatory Affairs Director
contributor.domain_expertise: PUC tariff filings, rate case management, interconnection agreements, regulatory docket tracking

choices: NEM-1 grandfathered — Conduit's reply brief in the NEM-2 rulemaking advocated for application date as enrollment, making this Conduit's own stated position
Cannot determine — the NEM-2 rule does not define 'enrolled' and no NEM-specific precedent exists; this must be escalated to the PUC for a declaratory ruling
NEM-2 applies — CC&B shows enrollment date of April 12, 2025, which is after the April 1 effective date; the system of record governs
NEM-1 grandfathered — the application was filed March 14, 2025, and Commission precedent (Decision 18-D-204) defines enrollment as application receipt date
